items.action: Patch MiCollab to 10.3 (10.3.0.18) plus KB000129195, Xen Orchestra to 5.213.1 or 5.211.2, and Juniper Session Smart to a fixed release before November 28, and check logs on exposed hosts.
items.details: Five of the 10 are MiCollab AWV flaws. Xen Orchestra CVE-2026-133469 (9.8) accepts an empty JSON object as a login cookie and gives admin access; Juniper CVE-2026-103406 (9.8) allows unauthenticated root command execution. CISA lists ransomware use as unknown for all 10.
items.summary: CISA added 10 actively exploited flaws to KEV on November 25, covering Mitel MiCollab, Vates Xen Orchestra, HPE Juniper Session Smart and Danfoss AK-SM 800A controllers. The worst is CVE-2026-133323 (CVSS 10.0), an unauthenticated blind OS command injection in MiCollab's AWV component; federal agencies must patch by November 28.
items.title: CISA adds 10 exploited flaws to KEV, Mitel MiCollab RCE at CVSS 10.0

items.action: Update vCenter to the fixed build for your branch now - note 9.x systems patched last week for CVE-2026-123890 still need this second update.
items.details: This is a separate flaw from CVE-2026-123890, the vmdir bypass exploited as a zero-day and patched November 19. Fixed versions are vCenter 9.1.2, 9.0.2.0300 and 8.0 U3m; Broadcom lists no workaround. The same advisory fixes 23 CVEs in total, including two 9.8 ESX I/O filter flaws.
items.summary: Broadcom's VMSA-2026-0011 (November 24) fixes CVE-2026-123903, a 9.8 authentication bypass in vCenter's VMware Directory Service reachable over LDAP. Rapid7 says a public proof of concept has been validated and urges urgent patching outside normal cycles, as attackers are already targeting vmdir flaws.
items.title: VMware vCenter auth bypass CVE-2026-123903 at 9.8, public PoC validated

items.action: Upgrade to 11.4.14, 11.3.23 or 10.6.23, run update.php, and block /core/install.php permanently; hunt logs for installer POSTs since November 18.
items.details: The original flaw, CVE-2026-132165, was added to CISA KEV on November 24 with a federal deadline of November 27 and was exploited on live sites from November 19. New fixed releases are Drupal 11.4.14, 11.3.23 and 10.6.23, and update.php must be run after upgrading.
items.summary: Drupal published SA-CORE-2026-019 on November 25 for CVE-2026-136716, confirming the November 18 fixes for the installer takeover flaw did not protect all sites in unusual or incomplete install states. Drupal rates it highly critical, lowered access complexity to basic, and reports exploitation in the wild.
items.title: Drupal follow-up CVE-2026-136716: first installer fix did not protect all sites

items.action: Apply the Fragnesia fixed build for your PAN-OS branch and remove the management interface from the internet - restrict it to trusted internal IPs or a VPN.
items.details: Bulletin PAN-SA-2026-0015 lists fixed builds across PAN-OS 10.2, 11.1, 11.2, 12.1 and 12.2. Palo Alto says customers already on a PHP2Shell-fixed build are protected, and all observed exploitation targeted devices with management interfaces exposed to the internet.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks released PAN-OS fixes on November 25 for Fragnesia (CVE-2026-46300), a Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw exploited to gain root on firewalls. The only known path chains it with the PHP2Shell flaws through an internet-exposed management interface.
items.title: Palo Alto patches Fragnesia flaw used to root PAN-OS firewalls

items.action: Watch for phishing using real names and sign-in emails - go to 1Password directly rather than clicking emailed recovery or invitation links, and never share Secret Keys or verification codes.
items.details: Stolen data includes names, email addresses, account and user IDs, creation and last sign-in times, public keys, SRP parameters and invitation, provisioning and account recovery tokens. The attacker also reached the CI/CD environment; exposed infrastructure credentials have been rotated or revoked and no account takeovers have been found.
items.summary: 1Password disclosed on November 25 that an attacker compromised an employee's corporate GitHub account, accessed private source code and pushed malicious code to backend services that downloaded customer account records for a subset of users. Customer vaults and the keys protecting them were not accessed.
items.title: 1Password discloses breach via compromised employee GitHub account

items.action: Apply the CVE-2026-16232 fix, restrict management access, and hunt for Run Script tasks with no matching SmartConsole login, a certificate named pivot.p12, or unloaded policies.
items.details: Post-compromise, the actor used a script for CVE-2026-16232, a SmartConsole authentication bypass, to launch over 100 management tasks - stealing firewall databases and internal CA files, minting a certificate and unloading security policies. Check Point says the flaw was disclosed in July with patches already available and is not new.
items.summary: GreyNoise reports an actor it tracks as GT13 compromised Check Point Security Management servers at 22 organisations, using a compromised Rejetto HFS server as a relay to collect data from 24 management servers. Confirmed activity ran from October 17 to November 2 and GreyNoise assesses AI-driven tooling was used, with low confidence on that point.
items.title: GT13 compromises 24 Check Point management servers at 22 organisations

items.action: Urbtix users should treat unexpected calls or messages claiming to be from Urbtix, organisers or banks as likely phishing and verify through official channels.
items.details: The contractor reported the intrusion on November 24 and took immediate containment measures. Urbtix does not store identity document data and credit card information is masked. The department has reported the incident to police, the Security Bureau, the Digital Policy Office and the privacy commissioner, and affected users are being notified.
items.summary: Hong Kong's Leisure and Cultural Services Department said on November 25 that hackers illegally accessed the Urbtix ticketing system, with preliminary findings suggesting personal data of about 1.3 million users is involved - usernames or names, telephone numbers and email addresses.
items.title: Urbtix Hong Kong breach affects about 1.3 million users

items.action: Treat as an unverified actor claim; education-sector teams should note the pattern of Pixelleaks targeting Indian institutions and check perimeter exposure.
items.details: This is one of three Indian Pixelleaks listings on November 24, alongside NKN Delhi PoP and Copperstone Clothing. Leak-site listings are the group's own assertions, not confirmed breaches.
items.summary: Ransomware group Pixelleaks listed IIM Raipur perimeter (Indian Institute of Management, iimraipur.ac.in) on its leak site on November 24, claiming a verified set of business records including personnel and operational material scheduled for publication. The claim has not been independently verified and no IIM Raipur statement was cited.
items.title: Pixelleaks claims IIM Raipur perimeter attack (unverified)

items.action: Treat as an unverified actor claim and monitor for any published material referencing Copperstone operations ahead of the November 28 deadline.
items.details: The leak post indicates a data disclosure threat; it does not claim systems were encrypted, and no screenshots or downloadable files were indicated in the report.
items.summary: Pixelleaks published a post on November 24 naming Copperstone Clothing Company, an Indian garment manufacturer and exporter, claiming business, financial, client and operational records reportedly linked to its SQL Server ERP environment, with a publication deadline of November 28 at 21:33 UTC. No ransom amount was stated and the claim is unverified.
items.title: Pixelleaks claims Copperstone Clothing, publication deadline November 28 (unverified)

items.action: Fintech teams should follow the police advisory in the report: caller authentication on payout APIs, effective IP allow-listing, no exposed production API docs, transaction limits and rate limiting.
items.details: Police say he gained unauthorised access to the company's electronic ledger and bank-linked payment gateway without valid credentials, and set up VPN nodes at his home for overseas associates. A laptop, router, Raspberry Pi, memory card and phone were seized; links to digital arrest fraud are also being probed. Reported November 25.
items.summary: Navi Mumbai Cyber Police arrested a Chennai-based engineer on November 18 for alleged involvement in a syndicate that siphoned Rs 1.98 crore from a fintech company by hacking its server from Hong Kong and manipulating its payment gateway. Police have frozen more than Rs 1 crore and say he was paid in cryptocurrency.
items.title: Navi Mumbai: Chennai engineer arrested in Rs 1.98 crore fintech hacking case

subtitle: Thursday, November 26 - CISA adds 10 exploited flaws, 1Password discloses a breach, and Pixelleaks claims two more Indian victims.
title: Morning Cybersecurity Digest
